answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on reachable, independently vouched paths rather than raw identities. A Sybil cluster with few links to honest nodes sits behind a sparse external cut: its low conductance limits walk flow across the boundary and, through min-cut transitivity bounds, caps its aggregate voting weight. A relic account, summit, or ridge of aliases cannot bypass that bottleneck without earning attestations from outside.
